title: The Offer
source: spec/socket-draft-00.md (doc rev 39), spec/ERRATA.md, spec/DECISIONS.md, registry/generated/registry.json, reference/python/bnap_ref.py
header: Offers are TLV streams signed by an online offer key (draft-00 section 4).
Offers are signed with SHA-256("bnap test offer key"), as in vectors.json, and carry a MAC
under SHA-256("bnap test mac key") unless the case says otherwise. Times are Unix seconds;
every expiry check allows 60 seconds of skew. A client cannot check the MAC.

Valid.description: A well-formed input every implementation must accept.

Structure.description: A record missing, of the wrong length or with a bad value.

ClassRule.description: An offer no gate may build: a binding-class, metering or quota rule of 4.3, 7, 12 or DECISIONS row 25 is broken. No socket code names this; the cases use MALFORMED, the code a validator reports.

Signature.description: offer_sig does not verify, or the key is not trusted.

Mac.description: The MAC does not verify under any current or retained key.

Expired.description: Expired, or issued in the future, beyond the 60 s skew.

Skew.description: Exactly at the edge of the 60 s skew allowance.

Scope.description: The offer names another action or route.

NotOffered.description: The credential uses a scheme the offer does not list.

Order.description: Two faults at once: the 4.4 order decides the code.

Tofu.description: No pinned manifest: the client trusts on first use.

Advance.description: An offer published in advance: no MAC, issued_at, a key the gate holds.

UnknownScheme.description: An entry whose scheme the client does not know, which it ignores.

UnknownOdd.description: An unknown odd record, ignored by the receiver.
